editorial:
Imagine walking straight into a painting. That is exactly what happens here. You follow a young man who travels to a small town to deliver a letter from the famous painter Vincent van Gogh. As he talks to the people who knew Vincent, you get to see the artist's final days through their eyes. The whole movie is painted by hand in the style of Van Gogh, which makes it feel like a dream. It is a slow, moody story that feels more like a mystery than a history lesson, and it really makes you wonder who Vincent actually was.

What really blows you away is the look of the film. Every single frame is a piece of art, and while the story is a bit slow, the visuals keep you glued to the screen. If you like art or a good mystery, you have to check this out.
endingExplained: You find out that Vincent did not commit suicide, but actually shot himself after a long struggle with his mental health and feeling like a failure. The movie wraps up by showing that while the world did not appreciate his art while he was alive, he is now one of the most loved painters in history. It ends on a sad but peaceful note, showing his legacy living on through his beautiful work.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves art, history, or unique visual styles.
